solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rodent lived so many years in Cyprus

indicators.note: the years-lived abbreviation sits within the Cyprus code, the clue placing one in the other

parts.note: CY is the international vehicle code for Cyprus
a.v. abbreviates Latin annos vixit, 'lived so many years', seen on gravestones

explanation.surface: A rodent that lived for some years on Cyprus.
explanation.walkthrough: AV for annos vixit is an epitaph abbreviation solvers may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: The guinea pig and its South American relatives are small rodents of this name.

clue.text: Automatic authorisation that might be dated

definitions.meaning: approval given routinely without real scrutiny
an inked hand stamp can print the date on a document

explanation.surface: Approval given without thought, which may carry a date.
explanation.definitionFit: Routine approval without consideration is idiomatically called this; literally the tool is an inked stamping device that often prints dates.

clue.text: Tease fractious lad who's vulgar

parts.note: to rib someone is to tease them

indicators.note: an unruly, fractious lad has his letters thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Teasing a bad-tempered boy who is coarse.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe humour that is crude and coarse, especially about sex.

clue.text: What turnstiles do for highest number of contestants

definitions.meaning: turnstiles count and log each person coming in
the largest field ever to compete in an event

explanation.surface: A description of turnstiles at a big competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as verb plus noun it is logging admissions; as adjective plus noun it is an unprecedentedly large field of competitors.

clue.text: Belgium's bird dog

parts.note: B is the international vehicle code for Belgium
the eagle is a bird of prey

explanation.surface: A bird dog belonging to Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird dog' reads as one phrase, a gun dog, but 'bird' is wordplay and 'dog' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hound bred for hunting hares is a breed of dog.

clue.text: With plumber I struggle to loosen muscles

indicators.note: the plumber and I struggle, so those letters are wrestled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A plumber and I struggle to warm up our muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: Stretching and warming up before exercise is a phrasal verb meaning to make the body supple.

clue.text: Only leader of expedition found on island

parts.note: 'but' can mean only, as in 'but a child'

indicators.note: the leader of the word expedition is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Only the head of an expedition turned up on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: An island in the Firth of Clyde in western Scotland.

clue.text: Comic Albert leaving American city

indicators.note: Albert leaving the city means his short name is taken out of it

parts.note: Buffalo is a city in New York State
Al is the usual short form of Albert

explanation.surface: A comedian named Albert leaves a US city.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic singer in opera, especially Italian opera buffa, is given this term.

clue.text: Not left in place of worship or place of unsurpassed beauty

indicators.note: 'Not left' means the left abbreviation is removed from the building

parts.note: a temple is a place of worship

explanation.surface: Not leaving a place of worship, or a place of great beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vale of Tempe in Thessaly was celebrated by classical poets as a beautiful valley, hence any lovely spot.

clue.text: Entertain Australian, one of a group of nine

parts.words: one of a group of nine
parts.note: there were nine Muses in Greek myth

explanation.surface: Entertaining an Australian who belongs to a group of nine.
explanation.definitionFit: To divert or delight someone is synonymous with entertaining them.

clue.text: Reason for not being forgotten

parts.note: the thing someone is remembered for, their one notable achievement

explanation.surface: Why someone stays remembered.
explanation.definitionFit: The feature or achievement for which a person becomes known keeps them in memory.

clue.text: Youngster coming back with personal hygiene problem is a lout

indicators.note: the youngster coming back means his word is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: a boy is a youngster
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A youth returning with body odour is a hooligan.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for an uncouth, aggressive young man, a hooligan.

clue.text: Using this one takes turns to get drier

definitions.text: Using this one takes turns to get drier

parts.words: Using this one takes turns to get drier
parts.note: a continuous looped cloth on a rod is rotated to reach a dry section

explanation.surface: Seemingly about people queuing in turn to dry off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes turns' suggests sharing; really the cloth is rolled round to bring a dry part into reach.
explanation.definitionFit: A looped cloth hung on a rotating rod in washrooms is pulled round to expose a fresh dry stretch.

clue.text: Everybody on southern side of the Channel

definitions.text: Everybody on southern side of the Channel

parts.words: Everybody on southern side of the Channel
parts.note: everybody as said in France, south across the English Channel

explanation.surface: Seemingly all the people living in France.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means 'everybody' in French, the language spoken across the Channel from England.
explanation.definitionFit: The French expression for 'everyone' or 'the whole world'.

clue.text: Stealthily progress down spiral staircase?

parts.note: to move along a twisting route, literally and as a gradual, sinuous progress

explanation.surface: Creeping quietly down a corkscrew stair.
explanation.definitionFit: To proceed along a twisting course, as one must on a spiral stair, is this idiom.

clue.text: Kinky girl put sex appeal into novel

indicators.note: sex appeal is put into the girl's name, one piece inside the other

parts.note: Lola is the girl in the Kinks' song of that name
IT is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A perverse girl puts some sexiness into a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kinky' points at the band the Kinks, whose 1970 hit is named after a girl, Lola.
explanation.definitionFit: Nabokov's 1955 book is a famous work of fiction.

clue.text: Char found French horn in southern Switzerland

indicators.note: the French horn is found in the southern-plus-Swiss letters, one piece within the other

parts.note: CH is the international code for Switzerland
cor is French for horn

explanation.surface: A French horn discovered in the south of Switzerland gets charred.
explanation.definitionFit: To burn or blacken a surface is to singe or char it.

clue.text: Financial advisers cut up fruit

parts.note: CAs are chartered accountants, who advise on money
to hew is to cut or chop up

explanation.surface: Financial advisers chopping up some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The kidney-shaped seed of a tropical tree is botanically a fruit, though eaten as a nut.

clue.text: Seasonal?

parts.note: belonging to one particular season, the fall of the year

explanation.surface: A one-word question about something to do with the seasons.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'Seasonal' is narrowed to just one season.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the fall of the year is a specific kind of seasonal.

clue.text: Introduced various tenders after independence

indicators.note: the jumbled tenders come after the independence letter, fixing the order

parts.note: I abbreviates independence or independent

indicators.note: the tenders are of various kinds, so their letters are arranged variously

explanation.surface: Assorted bids put forward once independence came.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something into place within another thing is to introduce it.

clue.text: Hybrid citrange undergoing chemical change

indicators.note: a hybrid mixes things together, here the letters of citrange

explanation.surface: A citrange, a hybrid citrus fruit, is changing chemically.
explanation.walkthrough: A citrange is a real hybrid of citron-type orange and trifoliate orange, so 'Hybrid' reads naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: Substances in the process of a chemical change are said to be combining or responding.

clue.text: Effort required from fielding side?

definitions.meaning: in cricket the fielding side aims to dismiss every batsman, leaving the other team with none in

explanation.surface: Total commitment demanded of a cricket team in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batting team is dismissed when ten batsmen are out; that is what the fielding side seeks.
explanation.definitionFit: Total effort is described idiomatically as an unrestrained push; in cricket the phrase describes a dismissed batting side.

clue.text: Second unit taking engineers' vessel

parts.note: B is second, as in B-grade or the second letter
I, the Roman numeral one, is a unit
REME is the British Army's Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers

explanation.surface: A second military unit commandeers the engineers' boat.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient galley with two banks of oars is a type of ship.

clue.text: Middle course taken by lucky agency

parts.note: happy can mean lucky, as in a happy chance
a medium is a means or agency by which something is done

explanation.surface: A compromise route chosen by a fortunate firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A satisfactory compromise between extremes is idiomatically the golden mean.

clue.text: Seething when there's a bubble on the surface

parts.note: a boil is an inflamed swelling on the skin's surface

explanation.surface: A liquid seething as bubbles break its surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bubble on the surface' suggests boiling water but means a skin swelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Bubbling hot or furious, the state of liquid heated to boiling point.

clue.text: Song performed deadpan day after day removed

indicators.note: the deadpan letters are performed in a new arrangement
the day letters are removed from the deadpan before rearranging

parts.note: D abbreviates day, and one day after another gives two of them

explanation.surface: A song delivered without expression, with days taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' takes both Ds from DEADPAN, leaving EAPAN, which 'performed' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymn of praise or triumph is a kind of song.

clue.text: Bird, not British, removed blouse!

indicators.note: the blouse is removed, its letters disturbed into a new order
'not British' means the British letter is dropped from the blouse

explanation.surface: A bird took off a blouse, though not a British one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not British' drops B from BLOUSE, leaving LOUSE, which 'removed' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The blackbird is called this in older English, and it also names the water dipper.

clue.text: Headline item, 'put down first card'

definitions.meaning: the main story in a newspaper or bulletin
in card games, to play the opening card of a trick

explanation.definitionFit: The top news story and the opening play in a card trick share this word.

clue.text: Try to separate two who show up in the middle

parts.note: to come is to arrive or show up
between means in the middle of two things

explanation.surface: Someone tries to part two people who turn up in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To interfere in a relationship and divide a couple is to intrude upon them.

clue.text: Fourth Maori dance, capital

parts.note: D is the fourth letter of the alphabet
the haka is a Maori war dance

explanation.surface: A fourth Maori dance in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Bangladesh.

clue.text: Individual not involved in final outcome filled case of pastry

indicators.note: the word final's letters come out as a different arrangement
the individual is not involved, so that letter is taken out of the word final

parts.note: I is a single individual, one person

explanation.surface: An individual with no part in the final result, beside a pastry case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not involved in' drops I from FINAL, leaving FNAL, which 'outcome' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An open tart of pastry holding a sweet or savoury filling is this dish.

clue.text: Stick the lady in second half of parade

indicators.note: the lady is placed in the half-parade letters, one piece inside the other
the second half of the six-letter word parade is its final three letters

parts.note: her refers to a woman, the lady

explanation.surface: A woman holding firm partway through a procession.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling or remain attached to something is a synonym of sticking.
